title: Answers cite even when the lawyer's text names sections in words
goal: Hulft's promise is that every answer cites the text it rests on. On 2026-11-21 an answer (chat fa91b05a: a review of a pasted Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, 19 steps, 33 tool calls, 15,335 characters) came back with no citations at all; the user: 'I see answer without citations? Are we kidding now?' and 'we need to fix it'. Fix the cause in the main agent's system prompt (user: 'isn't it better give proper system prompt'; prompt fix only, no rewrite, since a rewrite would show the answer, remove it and regenerate it).
for_whom: A lawyer who pastes a document (a contract, a policy, a plaint) that names sections in plain words and asks Hulft about it, in a quick chat or a case chat.

done_check.check: The main agent's prompt (packages/ai/src/agents/main.setup.ts) states the citation rule where it weighs most (at the end of the law sections, before the case) and says plainly that text the lawyer pastes or uploads may name sections in words, and the answer still cites each provision or passage it relies on as [[id]]. The prompt tests (build.test.ts) still pass, and the case chat's prompt keeps its sections after the law ones (prompt cache).

On the brief's own database, the question that failed (the second-review prompt of chat fa91b05a with the two pasted documents) is asked once after the change: the answer has citations (the 'N citations checked' line, N recorded) and its cost is recorded in the progress.
eval-chat is run once after the change: gold citations at least as before (20/20 at its last recorded run) and cost per question recorded; a miss is diagnosed before it is reported.

scenarios.steps: A lawyer pastes a client's agreement that refers to 'section 5 of the Rent Act' and 'Article 12' and asks which clauses are enforceable.
scenarios.expect: The answer cites the sections and articles it relies on as citations that open in the viewer, not as plain words copied from the agreement.

out_of_scope: Rewriting an uncited answer, or holding text back until a citation appears (user chose the prompt fix only).
A warning on an answer that cites nothing (offered, not chosen).
Changing the main model or its providers.
Checking that each citation supports its sentence.

decisions.note: Prompt fix only (user), after 'rewrite will show answer in UI and again remove and regen'. Diagnosis: the stored message of chat fa91b05a has 33 tool calls and 0 [[ markers (the chat before it, 9de3d72c, has 15); 19 of 20 steps, so the normal prompt, not the last-step note; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash via DeepInfra. The pasted documents cited sections in words ('section 23', 'section 26(3)(b)') and the answer did the same.

progress.note: Agreed; issue #87; branch app/uncited-answers off origin/main; Neon branch agent/uncited-answers (.env.local points at it, production kept as .env.main).

d1: the citation rule was already in 'How you write', the last law section before the case, so it stays there; added two bullets at its end: pasted or uploaded text may name sections in words, 'never cite in words'; and a check before sending that every statement of law carries an [[id]]. build.test.ts asserts both lines are in a plain and a case chat's prompt, before the closing lines (10/10 pass; ai 48 tests).

d2: the failing question (the round-2 review prompt with the same two pasted documents, scratchpad terms.txt + privacy.txt) asked once on local dev against agent/uncited-answers, test account, headed browser: chat 459ada69, 15 steps, 19 searches, 44 provisions, 6 amendment checks; 25 citations checked, 5 not verified (was 0 and 0 in fa91b05a); cost $0.0142 ($0.0164 billed), deepinfra.

d3: eval-chat 4,6,7,8,10,11,14,16,17 (the 9-question set of PIPELINE.md 2026-10-20 and 10-27; the brief's '20/20' baseline was wrong, the recorded runs are 9/9 on these 9; user approved this one run): hits 9/9; unread cites 10 (q6 3, q8 4, q17 3; the recorded runs had 5 and 9, one run each, so noise and the new 'every statement carries an [[id]]' line are not separated); 48 calls, 82% cached, $0.0220 in all ($0.0024 a question; recorded $0.0118-0.0148), slowest 32 s. A first run without the question list ran only the default 'dl' question ($0.0100, 20 cited, 2 unread): my slip, not a result. Log: scratchpad eval-chat9.log.

Validated on acfa0dd: semantic PASS (minor: wrong '20/20' baseline, disclosed; unread cites 10 vs 5-9 not separated; 5 of 25 citations in the d2 answer not verified), security PASS (no findings; no injection probe, paid). PR #88 rebase-merged; Vercel deploys main. Neon branch agent/uncited-answers deleted. Merged.
